# Feel Your Protocol MCP Server — Use Layer (full text)
# Source: mcp-docs/use/ — end-user documentation for humans and AI agents
# https://mcp-docs.feelyourprotocol.org/llms-full.txt

================================================================================
INTRODUCTION
================================================================================

Status: MCP docs site live. Remote MCP endpoint and gateway — not shipped yet.

Feel Your Protocol is building a headless MCP server that wraps the EthereumJS
stack so AI agents can run exact, deterministic simulations of the future
Ethereum protocol — upcoming forks, EIPs, and research — and receive rich JSON
traces they can reason over.

Mental model: the explorations website is the textbook; the MCP server is the
lab equipment. Vision and draft concepts: roadmap.feelyourprotocol.org

================================================================================
CAPABILITIES
================================================================================

Status: Bytecode simulation in progress (engine v0.1 local). Gateway tools and
remote endpoint — not live yet.

Intent-driven tools — verbs matching how agents think about protocol work:

- Simulate: Run raw bytecode under a fork/EIP configuration; optional trace.
  Status: Engine v0.1 (local)
- Compare: Run multiple variants (each with own fork + bytecode) and diff.
  Status: Engine v0.1 (local)
- Generate: Produce structured outputs such as block-level access lists.
  Status: Planned
- Probe: Describe supported forks, EIPs, limits. Status: Planned

Scope boundaries:
- Stateless / BYOS — caller supplies bytecode and state overrides
- Raw bytecode, base-layer only — no Solidity compilation
- Observability first — rich execution traces
- Hard wall — no multi-block historical backtesting

================================================================================
CONNECT
================================================================================

Status: Remote MCP endpoint NOT live yet. Gateway (stdio) — Step 3.

Endpoints:
- https://mcp-docs.feelyourprotocol.org — documentation (live)
- https://mcp.feelyourprotocol.org/mcp — remote MCP over HTTP (planned)

Connection steps will be documented when the gateway ships.

================================================================================
TOOL: SIMULATE BYTECODE
================================================================================

Status: Engine v0.1 (local). MCP tool simulate_evm_bytecode — planned Step 3.

Purpose: Run raw EVM bytecode under a fork/EIP configuration. Returns gas used,
return data, final stack, optional opcode trace, and provenance.

When to use:
- Test bytecode under upcoming fork or à la carte EIP set
- Inspect stack-level execution with optional trace
- Compare behaviour across fork configurations

Inputs:
- bytecode (required): hex-encoded, 0x prefix optional
- fork (optional): { baseHardfork, eips[] }
- gasLimit (optional): default 1_000_000
- trace (optional): include stack-only execution steps when true

Outputs:
- success: boolean
- gasUsed: string
- returnValue: hex
- finalStack: hex strings
- error: string or null
- steps: optional trace
- provenance: always present (engine version, fork config, capability metadata)

Limits: see Guarantees section below.

================================================================================
COVERAGE
================================================================================

Fork configuration is à la carte: base hardfork plus optional EIP list. Named
forks (e.g. amsterdam) are curated shortcuts.

Registered capabilities (seed):
- EIP 8024 (new-capability): simulate, compare
- EIP 7883 (repricing): simulate, compare
- EIP 7928 (new-structure): generate, simulate
- EIP 7951 (new-capability): simulate, compare
- EIP 8141 (new-exec-model): simulate (not yet implemented)

================================================================================
GUARANTEES
================================================================================

What you can rely on:
- Deterministic execution — same bytecode + fork config → same result
- Stateless / BYOS — no archive node
- Provenance on every result — engine version, fork config, optional EIP metadata
- Guardrails — hard limits below

Limits:
- Max gas limit: 30_000_000
- Default gas limit: 1_000_000
- Max bytecode size: 24_576 bytes
- Max trace steps: 10_000

Out of scope: Solidity compilation, ERC/application-layer, multi-block backtesting.

================================================================================
PRICING
================================================================================

Status: Not shipped. x402 payment layer planned. See roadmap.feelyourprotocol.org.
